correctness.rationale: Exact characters T_q of coloured linear orders follow from the published Ehrenfeucht--Fraisse character theorem. The known pure-order rank-three 7-element saturation plus the concatenation lemma reduce all infinite parameter triples to exactly 512 cases. The bundled stdlib certificate exhaustively compares the proposed canonical form bidirectionally against exact nested rank-three character objects on those cases, obtaining 310 classes, the unique longest shortest key (6,5,6), and the sharp 19 bound. A separate direct game recursion tests 14 boundary pairs. The no-three-red rank-three formula rules out shorter equivalent words outside the two-red family. No probabilistic hash uniqueness, partial enumeration, or external computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A complete natural classification for finite linearly ordered structures with exactly two marked points and quantifier rank three, a first nontrivial step beyond the published one-red family. It determines the exact number 310 and the sharp finite minimal-representative bound 19, including the structural 5-versus-6 distinction between middle and exterior gaps. Prior papers motivate this explicitly by studying difficult optimal rank-three coloured orders; neither generic computability nor a one-red theorem supplies the exact two-red counts. The result is finite but uniform over arbitrarily long input words and includes a meaningful natural invariant rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
